Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_openrouter-minimax-minimax-m3_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_openrouter-minimax-minimax-m3_01.html`.
I'll build a complete CHIP-8 emulator in a single self-contained HTML file. Let me start by planning the work and then creating the file.

  1. `00CN` clear screen (N=0: clear, N=1: return from subroutine / set PC from stack)
  2. `1NNN` jump to address NNN
  3. `2NNN` call subroutine at NNN
  4. `3NNN` skip if register Vx equals NNN
  5. `4XNN` skip if register Vx does not equal NNN
  6. `5XY0` skip if Vx == Vy
  7. `5XY1` skip if Vx != Vy
  8. `5XY2` skip if Vx < Vy
  9. `5XY3` skip if Vx > Vy
  10. `6XNN` set Vx = NN
  11. `7XNN` Vx += NN
  12. `8XY0` Vx = Vy
  13. `8XY1` Vx |= Vy
  14. `8XY2` Vx &= Vy
  15. `8XY3` Vx ^= Vy
  16. `8XY4` Vx += Vy with carry flag in VF
  17. `8XY5` Vx -= Vy with borrow flag in VF
  18. `8XY6` Vx <<= 1 (or Vx >>= 1 for 8XYE), VF = bit shifted out
  19. `8XY7` Vx >>= 1, VF = bit shifted out
  20. `8XY8` Vx = Vy + Vy (commonly 8XY8/8XY9/8XYA/8XYB/8XYC/8XYD/8XYE/8XYF carry variants — handle the classic meanings: 8XY8 Vx=Vy+Vy, 8XY9 Vx=Vy+1, 8XYA Vx=Vy*2... keep it simple: implement the standard 8XY0–8XYF table used by most interpreters: 0, OR, AND, XOR, ADD(carry), SUB(borrow), SHR(flag), SHL(flag), plus 8XY9/8XYA/8XYB/8XYC/8XYD/8XYE/8XYF as skip-free/flag variants that at minimum must not break decoding)
  21. `9XY0` skip if Vx != Vy
  22. `AXYN` set I = NNN
  23. `BXYN` jump to NNN + V0
  24. `CXNN` Vx = random & NN
  25. `DXYN` draw sprite at (Vx, Vy) with N bytes of sprite data, XOR onto the framebuffer, set VF = 1 if any pixel was erased by collision; handle screen wrapping on both axes
  26. `EXNN` skip if key N is pressed
  27. `FXNN` skip if key N is not pressed
  28. `FX15` Vx = delay timer value
  29. `FX18` Vx = sound timer value
  30. `FX1A` Vx = value of key currently pressed (0..15), 0xFF if none
  31. `FX21` store V0..VF in memory at I (48 bytes) — and implement the matching `FX55` load V0..VF from memory at I
  32. `FX55` load V0..VF from memory at I
  33. `FX65` increment I (increase I by Vx)
  34. `FX75` set the sound timer to Vx
  35. `FX85` set the delay timer to Vx
  Use the standard `FX` group consistently: FX15 (read delay), FX18 (read sound), FX1A (get key), FX21 (set I += 32 style or screen-store — pick the classic "I = I + 32" for FX21 and "I = I + 32 + 1" for FX55 if you implement the hybrid, OR simply implement: FX21 = store V registers at I; FX55 = load V registers from I; FX65 = I += Vx) — be consistent and document it in a small on-page "instruction reference" list.
- Flags/carry/borrow stored in VF for `8XY4` (carry), `8XY5` (borrow), and shift-out bits for `8XY6`/`8XY7` (VF = 1 when the shifted-out bit was 1, else 0). NOTE: because VF is both a register and a flag, standard practice is that `8XY4`/`8XY5`/`8XY6`/`8XY7` write the flag to VF — implement that.
- `DXYN` must set VF to the collision flag (1 on collision, 0 otherwise) — and note this is the same VF.
- Unknown opcodes should be ignored gracefully (advance PC by 2) and counted/displayed, not crash.

## B. Display
- 64x32 pixel framebuffer (Uint8Array of 64*32, 0 or 1).
- Canvas scaled to a readable size (e.g. 10-12 px per pixel → 640x384, or set width/height attributes to 640x384 and use `image-rendering: pixelated` CSS). Include a CRT-ish look with a dark background and a phosphor green color, but keep it readable.
- Sprites drawn with XOR semantics; wrap coordinates at the edges.

## C. Keypad
- 16-key keypad (4x4 block) shown in the interface as clickable on-screen buttons labeled with the CHIP-8 hex key and the mapped keyboard key.
- Standard mapping: 
  row0: 1 2 3 C  → keyboard 1 2 3 4
  row1: 4 5 6 D  → keyboard Q W E R
  row2: 7 8 9 E  → keyboard A S D F
  row3: A 0 B F  → keyboard Z X C V
- Both key PRESS and key RELEASE must reach the emulator: maintain `keysPressed[16]` state; on keydown set true and record the "last pressed key" for FX1A; on keyup set false. Handle the browser repeat event (ignore `event.repeat` for the state change but keep it simple: only act when not repeating). Also handle window blur → clear all keys.
- Clicking on the on-screen keypad buttons must also press/release the corresponding key (mousedown = press, mouseup/mouseleave = release).

## D. Demo ROM
- Include a real hand-assembled demo ROM as a byte array literal in the file. It must:
  - draw a sprite (e.g. a 4x4 or 8x8 sprite defined in the program data area),
  - move a sprite in response to the arrow-ish keys (or move on a key press) — e.g. use FX0A (skip if key not pressed) to read the keypad and move V-position registers,
  - clear the screen and use an infinite loop.
  - Write it as a small assembler-like byte array with comments above the array showing the assembly source, e.g.:
    ```
    ; Draws a heart/arrow sprite and moves it with the keypad
    200: A230      LD I, 0x230       ; sprite data address
    202: 6108      LD V0, 8
    ...
    ```
  - The demo must work with the emulator's documented opcode semantics. Make the sprite data live at e.g. 0x230 in the ROM byte array so I points at real bytes.
  - Include an "assemble" helper inside the file? No — hardcode the byte array.

## E. Controls (every one must work)
- Run (start/resume), Pause, Single Step (executes exactly one instruction and updates the debugger), Reset (reloads the current ROM, clears memory/registers/framebuffer, resets PC to 0x200).
- Speed control: a range slider "Instructions per frame" (e.g. 1–100) plus a display of the value; also optionally a "frames per second"/step delay. Use requestAnimationFrame with an accumulator to run `ipf` instructions per frame.
- Load ROM from a local file: `<input type="file" accept=".ch8,.bin">` reading via FileReader as binary, loading at 0x200, then auto-reset. Also a "Load demo ROM" button. Show the current ROM name in the status bar.
- A "clear/blank" option is not required.

## F. Debugger panel
Show live:
- All 16 registers V0..VF in hex (2-digit) — highlight VF as the flag register.
- The index register I (hex, 4-digit) and the program counter PC (hex, 4-digit).
- The call stack: list of return addresses, most recent at top, showing depth; update as instructions execute.
- The decoded current instruction at PC: show opcode hex, the mnemonic (e.g. `LD V3, 0x42`, `JP 0x300`, `CALL 0x310`, `SHR V5`, `ADD V2, V7` with carry, `DRW V1, V2, 5`, `SKP V2`, etc.) and the raw bytes. The decoder must handle every opcode implemented and produce a readable mnemonic; unknown → "???".
- Delay timer and sound timer values.
- Also an optional small hex memory viewer (show 16 bytes around PC, with the PC byte highlighted) — nice-to-have but must work.
- Optionally show an instruction counter / executed-instruction count.

## G. UI/layout
- Modern, clean, responsive CSS (dark theme), no external fonts — use system font stack.
- Layout: header with title, main area with the screen on the left and the keypad + controls on the right, and the debugger panel below or beside. Use CSS grid/flex with a media query for narrow screens.
- Make the keypad visually clear: 4x4 grid of buttons, each showing the hex key and the keyboard mapping; highlight a key when it is pressed.
- A small help/legend section listing the key mapping and the implemented instruction set.
- Everything must be in the one file. No network requests at all.

## H. Quality requirements
- No syntax errors. Use `'use strict'`; avoid `var` where `let/const` works; use modern but widely-supported JS.
- Guard against `pc` running past the end of memory.
- Reset should also clear the timers and stack.
- The file must be fully self-contained and openable directly from the filesystem (file://) — so no modules, no fetch, no external assets.
- Add a brief comment header at the top of the file describing the emulator.
